eagle.title: Apollo 11 landing radio, July 20 1969: 'Contact light... Tranquility Base here, the Eagle has landed'
eagle.credit: NASA (Mission Control Public Affairs loop); clip via Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, courtesy John Stoll, NASA JSC

surveyor3.title: Apollo 12 radio, Nov 20 1969: Pete Conrad and Al Bean cut parts off Surveyor 3 ('Good cut... it's even got dirt in it!')
surveyor3.credit: NASA (Apollo 12 air-to-ground); clip via Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, Ken Glover

alsep.title: Apollo 12 radio, Nov 19 1969: Al Bean sets up the first ALSEP seismometer ('Here's hoping nothing happens to it')
alsep.credit: NASA (Apollo 12 air-to-ground); clip via Apollo Lunar Surface Journal

rover16.title: Apollo 16 radio, April 21 1972: John Young reads out the rover's batteries, 'and we're on our way', first drive to Station 1
rover16.credit: NASA (Apollo 16 air-to-ground); clip via Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, Roland Speth

insight.title: Wind on Mars, recorded by InSight's seismometer, Dec 1 2018 (raised two octaves so it is audible)

ingenuity.title: Ingenuity's rotor hum over Martian wind, recorded by Perseverance's SuperCam microphone on its 4th flight, April 30 2021

spirit.title: A Martian dust devil passing over Perseverance, recorded by its SuperCam microphone, Sept 27 2021 (stand-in: Spirit's own mission had no microphone; dust devils famously cleaned its solar panels)

opportunity.title: Wind on Mars, recorded by Perseverance's SuperCam microphone, Feb 22 2021 (stand-in: Opportunity had no microphone; a dust storm ended its mission)

viking1.title: First sounds ever recorded on Mars: muffled wind, Perseverance SuperCam, Feb 19 2021 (stand-in: Viking 1 had no microphone)

sojourner.title: A rover's wheels rolling on Mars: Perseverance driving in Jezero Crater, sol 16, March 2021, filtered highlights (stand-in: Sojourner had no microphone)

phoenix.title: A Mars lander creaking as it cools at sunset ('dinks and donks'), recorded by InSight's seismometer, July 16 2019 (stand-in: Phoenix carried a microphone but it never returned a sound; the polar winter froze it)
